pr_title: Add support for the Command Palette
pr_body:
## Summary of the Pull Request

![command-palette-001](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18356694/85313480-b6dbef00-b47d-11ea-8a8f-a802d26c2f9b.gif)


This adds a first iteration on the command palette. Notable missing features are:
* Commandline mode: This will be a follow-up PR, following the merge of #6537
* nested and iterable commands: These will additionally be a follow-up PR.

This is also additionally based off the addenda in #6532. 

This does not bind a key for the palette by default. That will be done when the above follow-ups are completed.

## References
* #2046 - The original command palette thread
* #5400 - This is the megathread for all command palette issues, which is tracking a bunch of additional follow up work 
* #5674 and #6532 - specs
* #6537 - related

## PR Checklist
* [x] Closes #2046
  - incidentally also closes #6645
* [x] I work here
* [x] Tests added/passed
* [ ] Requires documentation to be updated - delaying this until it's more polished.


## Detailed Description of the Pull Request / Additional comments

* There's a lot of code for autogenerating command names. That's all in `ActionArgs.cpp`, because each case is so _not_ boilerplate, unlike the rest of the code in `ActionArgs.h`.

## Validation Steps Performed

* I've been playing with this for months.
* Tests
* Selfhost with the team

issue_context.title: Make keys in the command palette look like actual keys, like in VS Code
issue_context.body:
Omitted from initial implementation in #6635.

Add little borders & boxes to really emphasize that the keys are _keys_ to press. I don't know how to do this in XAML, but I think it would be a bit of nice polish.
comments:
> Omitted from initial implementation in #6635.
> 
> Add little borders & boxes to really emphasize that the keys are _keys_ to press. I don't know how to do this in XAML, but I think it would be a bit of nice polish.

I think PowerToys does something similar with its Key Remapping.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7389110/85791420-b10a3600-b729-11ea-8434-e1052cdee5d3.png)

Maybe you could decide on a "house style" to try to be consistent?

> Strong veto. When we have key _chords_ (as opposed to just key _notes_, see #1334), then we'll definitely want to keep the current design, for something like <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd>+<kbd>Ctrl+U</kbd>.

_from @zadjii-msft_

This is at odds with #1334 now. We currently have a version that displays each key _chord_ in its own pill.
When we have chords composed of notes (i.e, when implementing #1334), we should come back around to update this UI too 😉

:tada:This issue was addressed in #6635, which has now been successfully released as `Windows Terminal Preview v1.2.2022.0`.:tada:

I'm wondering if there's a better way of setting/updating the CommandPalette's current actions - though this is me thinking in terms of wanting to use all the functionality of CommandPalette but replacing CommandPalette Actions with a vector of SwitchToTab Actions.

Currently I can easily reuse this control for the TabSwitcher by calling `SetActions(tabCommands)`, but if my `vector<Command> tabCommands` ever changes (i.e. removal, addition, reordering, aka all tab stuff), it'd have to call SetActions for each modification. Maybe `_allActions` can be made to observe a "Commands Source" so that if my SwitchToTab commands are added to, removed from, reordered, etc, `_allActions` will update accordingly? Then theoretically, switching between TabSwitcherMode and CommandPaletteMode could be as easy as pointing _allActions to a different "Commands Source".
This doesn't seem like a terrible idea, though are you cool if we punt that for the v1 at least? That seems like refactoring we could come back through on a second pass and do 🤔
Oh yeah we can for sure punt it! 👍
We're adding MRU order at some point right? If so, maybe link the GitHub issue here?
now should _this_ become a `std::unordered_map`?
If I do the "sort alphabetically entries with the same weight" thing, then _yes_. If I just do the `unordered_map` without that, they're in _super random_ order.
no need for the intermediate temporary, right?

ParseAndLayerJsonCommands might be better
consider using a struct or pair that holds the 2 outputs instead of using the return + out param.
There's a `fmt::print(ss` overload, if you'd like to avail yourself of it

Do you cache these somewhere? I understand you have to generate them to work with the permutations of these types of actions, but I can't seem to find a cache of the resultant strings. I'm concerned about regenerating them on every open of the command palette. Am I missing something?

Oh yea, I can clear that up. These names are only generated for each action when we parse the settings. So they're generated once per action, per settings reload. Once the strings are generated, we'll hang on to them in the Command object (in it's `Name`) until the settings are reloaded.

FYI, `_UpperCase` tokens are reserved for the C++ language. consider alternative naming. see [this page](https://wiki.sei.cmu.edu/confluence/display/cplusplus/DCL51-CPP.+Do+not+declare+or+define+a+reserved+identifier#DCL51-CPP.Donotdeclareordefineareservedidentifier-NoncompliantCodeExample%28HeaderGuard%29) for details

Gonna be honest, I thought I wasn't going to like this. Now I feel that I can't live without it haha.

So I'm thinking about how a TabSwitcher would be able to navigate through panes, and wondering if the CommandPalette control can allow for a "secondary action". I.E. pressing enter on a tab would focus the tab (Command 1), but pressing right arrow while the tab is focused would bring up a flyout of the tab's panes (Command 2). This is definitely a thought experiment. I was just wondering what you thought and whether or not it's practical/feasible and whether it would benefit the command palette as well.

So there'll already be "nested commands", where you can hit enter on "New Tab...", and it'll switch the list to display "profile 1, profile 2, profile 3, etc...". That kind of model could also work for the tab switcher. It'd be easy to hook up the left/right arrows to do that as well. 

Displaying the nested commands w/in the parent `ListViewItem` might get harder, but it could _probably_ be done
